summary: Investigated ISS-2952 (cross-WIN H(r)-vs-B(r) terminology standardization flagged by curmudgeon WIN-040.c5). The two WINs named in the ISS (WIN-040, WIN-053) already carry the standardized frame -- the decider self-applied WIN-040 sibling ISS-2950/2951 in the same commit that created ISS-2952, and WIN-053 already ties H(r)/B(r) together via the shared lambda scale length. Extended the pass per the ISS routing_reason (check any other WIN invoking axial symmetry): found the canonical data/sections.json #axial-symmetry section (2.10 The Axial Symmetry Paradox), which 12+ WINs link to instead of re-deriving the point, itself mislabels H(r) as the domes core field equation -- the exact mislabel curmudgeon flagged. Patched that section once (2 patches) plus 3 WINs (WIN-041, WIN-043, WIN-059) independently found via grep to repeat the same field equation H(r) phrasing. 5 total patches, all verified unique-match + JSON-valid via local simulation before this proposal. No verdict changes; pure terminology tightening that preempts the defender semantic-swap (H(r) is firmament-height, not our field equation) documented in WIN-040.c5 advocate_mode.
